item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO – Well, enough of that – now on to the important stuff.
The Dodgers reached the end of the compulsory phase of their year, finishing the regular season with a 5-1 win in 10 innings against the San Francisco Giants on Sunday afternoon at Oracle Park.
The win was the Dodgers’ 100th of the season. It is the 12th time in franchise history that they have finished a season with 100 wins (including six of the past nine full seasons). None of the previous 100-win regular seasons were followed by a World Series championship.
The Dodgers will now take Monday off before getting together for four days of simulated games, live batting practice and whatever else they deem necessary to get ready for the opening of the postseason that will determine if they can become the first National League franchise to win three consecutive World Series championships.
Game 1 of their NL Division Series will be Saturday at Dodger Stadium against the winner of the Wild Card Series between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies. That best-of-three series begins Tuesday in Atlanta – and the Dodgers will be watching.
“There’s going to be some watch parties at the ballpark. I thought that was something that was really good,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the bye week itinerary established in 2024. “You’re not playing in the Wild Card Series, but you’re watching it and you kind of get your juices going. There’s also a bonding piece that I think is important.
“I thought we did a good job of having enough live and game situations, simulating them. Our coaches are sort of revisiting what we did a couple years ago. If there’s things we want to improve on or what – it worked out well a couple years ago. A lot of it’s also contingent on how guys are feeling, making sure they get rested and reset.”
MLB’s easiest September schedule allowed the Dodgers to go into their bye week with positive momentum. They went 18-7 in the final month (including 6-0 against the Giants in the final 10 days). Only the San Diego Padres (19-6) had more wins in the month.
Those bye-week sim games essentially started this weekend at Oracle Park.
On Sunday, the Dodgers sent seven pitchers to the mound to get their work. They allowed one run on five hits — and survived giving up the potential game-deciding home run. Giants shortstop Christian Koss took Dodgers reliever Bobby Miller deep leading off the eighth inning — but replay review turned the home run into a foul ball.
Roki Sasaki made his third appearance out of the bullpen since returning from a blister and did nothing to undermine his status as perhaps the most important bullpen weapon the Dodgers will have this postseason. He struck out two of the three batters he faced in a 1-2-3 inning.
Over his three innings in relief, Sasaki has faced 11 batters and struck out six, allowing two hits in his first appearance and none since.
“I think the fastball’s better,” Roberts said, comparing the version of Sasaki the Dodgers got when they moved him to the bullpen last postseason. “I think the split’s better. It’s also nice that he’s already done it. Just in total, he’s just a better pitcher than he was last year and a lot more confident.”
Edwin Diaz continued to affirm his status as a rediscovered bullpen weapon with another 1-2-3 inning. And Roberts reported Edgardo Henriquez has been throwing bullpen sessions this weekend and will participate in the bye week workouts with the expectation that he will be ready to return from his lower back injury and be part of the Dodgers’ NLDS bullpen.
The Dodgers’ offense didn’t spark to life until the 10th inning when Alex Call doubled in the free runner then trotted home on a three-run home run by Andy Pages.

item.content:encoded:
For nine-plus innings, the Dodgers and Giants couldn’t buy a hit with a runner in scoring position, but in the tenth, the Dodgers broke through for a 5-1 win. Alex Call and Andy Pages recorded two-out hits, a double, and a three-run shot to give the Dodgers their first lead in this game and the only one they’d need.
Dodgers find their breakthrough in extras to beat the Giants
Making a habit out of squandering chances through nine innings, the Dodgers scored four in extras to beat the Giants
Before getting to that point of being tied in extras, Jack Dreyer did a reasonable job of keeping the Giants at bay as an opener, but a stolen base allowed the opportunity for just a pair of singles to open the scoring in the second. Shay Whitcomb singled and stole second, later driven in by Scott Bandura—his first RBI of the season, playing in just his 13th big league game. Bandura also tried to steal a base, but this time Dreyer was alert to the danger and picked him off.
Facing a traditional bullpen game with Carson Seymour completing just one inning to open this one, the Dodgers first threatened to score in the third, the inning marked by Tony Vitello’s ejection. With two on and a 2-2 count to Mookie Betts, a check swing in which he probably went around was called a no-swing. Vitello came out to argue what had already been a topic of frustration earlier in the game and was thrown out for the seventh time in his 2026. The Giants, however, got out of the jam, as Betts struck out on the next pitch, and Sam Hentges also punched out Freddie Freeman.
What the Dodgers offense couldn’t do in the third, it did in the following frame. Kyle Tucker got on to leadoff the inning thanks to a defensive error by the second baseman and moved to third on a Max Muncy double—his 27th of the season, setting a new career high in a single season. With two on and one out, Andy Pages evened the score with a sacrifice fly.
Through the following innings, the Dodgers kept threatening but never coming through, first with a Freddie Freeman hit with a man on being taken away by a great defensive play from Jonah Cox—somewhat redeeming himself for the error that contributed to the Dodgers’ first run. That, by the way, would be Freeman’s last action in the game, replaced after five by Kiké Hernández as Dave Roberts rotated key pieces.
In the sixth, Muncy nearly wrote another chapter in his book as a giant killer. But the deepest part of the park was just deep enough to keep him from a solo shot in a ball that would’ve gone out in 23 of 30 stadiums. Perhaps the biggest squandered chance, though, came in the seventh and eighth when the Dodgers first stranded a leadoff double by Tommy Edman with three straight groundouts—an inning later, after Muncy secured his third hit of the day, Andy Pages hit into an inning-ending double play with two on and one out.
The Dodgers’ pitching was the reason the offense kept getting these opportunities to take the lead. Justin Wrobleski was the first pitcher out of the bullpen for the Dodgers, but looking for an even distribution of workload, he only completed two scoreless innings in under 30 pitches. Roki Sasaki and Edwin Díaz combined to strike out three, each with a scoreless frame.
Although Wrobleski had a couple of scares, the Giants truly came back to threaten again in the seventh when Bobby Miller took the mound, but also without actually breaking through. With runners at the corners and no outs, Miller secured a strikeout, then lucked into Marcelo Mayer staying at third on a wild pitch quickly recovered by Hunter Feduccia, recorded another punchout, and finished off the inning with a groundout.
With both teams exhausting new ways of threatening without actually scoring, the Giants looked like they’d take the lead with a leadoff bomb in the eighth by Christian Koss. However, the call on the field of a home run was overturned when replay made it clear it was a foul ball, and the score remained 1-1 through nine innings.
Even in the tenth, it looked like the Dodgers were going to strand the ghost runner after their first two hitters were retired without him advancing to third, but Call came through, and an intentional walk later, Pages had the big hit of the game. With the four RBI he recorded in this game, Pages left Ohtani behind and isolated himself as the Dodgers’ RBI leader this season, with 85.
Sunday particulars
Home run: Andy Pages (23)
WP —Alex Vesia (3-1): 1 IP, 1 hit, 1 strikeout
LP —Duncan Davitt (0-1):1 IP, 2 hits, 4 runs, 3 earned runs, 1 walk
Up next
The Dodgers get a little under a week off before they get back on the field on Saturday at home. They’ll be playing host to the winner of the Wild Card round between the Braves and Phillies in game 1 of the NLDS. No starters have been announced for that series.
